issues.t: Camshaft position sensor can melt and start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: A burning plastic smell or smoke from under the hood, often with the check engine light on. Some owners also had rough running, stalling or a no-start.
issues.why: The camshaft position sensor, which tells the engine computer where the camshaft is, can overheat and melt. The heat can spread to the cam cover and the sensor wiring and could start a fire. Recalls 04V-357 and 04V-394 replace the sensor and add a fuse. Several owners reported fires.
issues.next: If you smell burning or see smoke, pull over, turn the engine off and get everyone away from the car. Daewoo's US dealers closed soon after the recall, so many cars never got the fix. Call NHTSA's recall line with your VIN, and ask a shop to check the sensor, fuse and wiring.

issues.t: Timing belt breaks and bends valves
issues.sym: The engine suddenly quits while driving and then cranks but won't start. Some owners heard a slap or rattle first.
issues.why: The 2.0L engine uses a rubber timing belt, and it is an engine where the valves hit the pistons if the belt snaps. Owners reported belts breaking between about 45,000 and 71,000 miles, often leading to bent valves. A leaking water pump or a worn tensioner can ruin the belt early.
issues.next: If you have no record of it, have the timing belt, tensioner, idler pulleys and water pump replaced now. Daewoo owners suggest doing it about every 55,000 miles. If the belt has already broken, don't keep cranking. Have the car towed and ask for a compression or leak-down test before deciding on repairs.

issues.t: Front lower control arm bushings wear out
issues.sym: The car pulls or darts to one side, jerks sideways when you get on or off the gas, shakes at highway speed, or eats the front tires. Some owners heard a squeak, creak or clunk from the front end.
issues.why: The rubber bushings in the front lower control arms wear out early on this car, sometimes before 20,000 to 30,000 miles. Loose arms let the wheels shift under power and braking, which also throws off the alignment.
issues.next: Have the front suspension inspected for torn or loose bushings and worn ball joints. Replacing the control arms or bushings, then getting an alignment, usually cures the pulling and tire wear.

issues.t: Front brake hoses can crack and leak (recall)
issues.sym: Brake fluid on the inside of a front wheel, a falling fluid level, or a brake pedal that feels soft or sinks.
issues.why: Some front brake hoses did not meet the federal brake hose standard. The outer rubber layer can crack, and the hose can burst and leak fluid, cutting braking power. Recall 02V-257 installs redesigned hoses.
issues.next: If the pedal feels soft or you see a leak, don't drive the car. Check with NHTSA using your VIN to see if the recall was done. If not, have a shop fit new front brake hoses and bleed the brakes.

issues.t: Brake pedal sinks toward the floor
issues.sym: The brake pedal feels spongy or slowly sinks to the floor during a stop, and the car takes longer to stop. A few owners reported crashes.
issues.why: Owners traced this to leaking brake hoses, corroded brake lines and failing master cylinders. In some cases, a master cylinder was replaced and the problem came back.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Treat this as urgent. Don't drive if the pedal goes low. Have the whole brake system checked, including the hoses, steel lines, calipers and master cylinder, and have any leak fixed before driving again.

issues.t: Engine surges or revs on its own
issues.sym: The engine revs up by itself at a stop or in Park, the car lunges when shifted into Drive, or it surges when you lift off the gas. Some owners had to switch the engine off.
issues.why: NHTSA reports don't name one cause. On fuel-injected engines of this age, a dirty throttle body, a sticking idle control valve or a vacuum leak are common reasons for a high or surging idle.
issues.next: If the car surges, hold the brake firmly, shift to Neutral and turn the engine off once you're safely stopped. Have a shop check the idle control valve, throttle body, vacuum hoses and any trouble codes before driving it again.

issues.sym: The check engine light comes on and stays on, or flickers on and off. Some cars ran rough, lost power or failed emissions inspection.
issues.why: Many owners found the camshaft position sensor at fault. Others had a misfire code, an oxygen sensor or a knock sensor. Some lights stayed on even after the recall sensor was fitted.
issues.next: Have the trouble codes read. If the code points to the camshaft sensor, also check whether the recall work was done. Don't ignore a flashing light, which means a misfire that can damage the catalytic converter.

issues.t: Engine stalls at low speed or idle
issues.sym: The engine dies when coming to a stop, at very low speed or with the lights and fan on. It may restart, or it may stall on the highway.
issues.why: Owners linked stalling to the failing camshaft sensor, fuel delivery problems and electrical faults. The exact cause varies from car to car.
issues.next: If the car stalls in traffic, put on the hazard lights and steer to safety; the steering and brakes will be heavier. Have it scanned for codes and checked for the recall sensor, fuel pressure and wiring problems.

issues.t: Automatic transmission fails or won't move
issues.sym: The car won't move in Drive even though the engine runs, gets stuck in one gear, or downshifts suddenly at speed and won't upshift.
issues.why: Owners reported automatic transmission failures from about 50,000 to 75,000 miles. The cause isn't documented in detail, but worn internal parts and low or old fluid are usual reasons.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. If it is low, dark or smells burnt, or the car won't move, don't keep driving. Have a transmission shop check for codes and fluid problems before agreeing to a rebuild.

issues.t: Brake rotors warp and pads wear fast
issues.sym: Grinding or squealing brakes, a shaking steering wheel or pedal when stopping, and pads and rotors that need replacing very often.
issues.why: Many owners had to resurface or replace front rotors and pads again and again, sometimes every few thousand miles. Worn control arm bushings can add to the shimmy.
issues.next: Have the brakes inspected for thin pads, warped rotors and sticking calipers. Good-quality pads and rotors, plus checking the front suspension bushings, usually help.

issues.sym: Oil spots under the car, a burning oil smell, smoke from the engine bay, or an oil level that drops between changes. A few owners lost up to a quart or more a day.
issues.why: Owners reported leaks from the valve cover gasket, the oil pump at the front of the engine and the head gasket. Oil from the front of the engine can also soak the timing belt and shorten its life.
issues.next: Check the oil level weekly until it's fixed. Have a shop find where the leak starts; if it's at the front of the engine, ask them to check the timing belt for oil damage.

issues.sym: The temperature gauge climbs, white smoke from the exhaust, coolant loss, oil leaks or the engine stalling.
issues.why: A few owners reported head gasket failures and overheating. Overheating the aluminum head can warp it and blow the gasket.
issues.next: If the gauge rises, pull over and turn off the engine. Don't open the radiator cap while hot. Have the cooling system pressure-tested and the head gasket checked before driving further.

issues.t: Starts and dies, or cranks with no spark
issues.sym: The engine cranks but never fires, or it starts and then shuts off right away as if a security system stopped it.
issues.why: Owners suspected the crankshaft position sensor, which the engine computer needs to make spark, or the anti-theft system. Loose sensor connectors can cause the same no-start.
issues.next: Have a shop check for spark and fuel while the problem is happening, and test the crank and cam sensors and their plugs. Try the spare key in case the key chip is the problem.

issues.t: Brake lights fail and shifter sticks in Park
issues.sym: The brake lights don't come on when you press the pedal, or the shifter won't come out of Park.
issues.why: A failed brake light switch at the pedal cuts the brake lights and also the signal that releases the shift lock.
issues.next: Have someone check your brake lights. If they're out, get the brake light switch replaced soon, since drivers behind you can't see you stopping.

issues.sym: A humming, grinding or roaring noise from a front wheel that rises with speed, sometimes with clanking or vibration.
issues.why: Owners reported front wheel bearings wearing out early, around 57,000 miles in one case.
issues.next: Have the wheel bearings checked soon. A badly worn bearing can overheat and let the wheel wobble.

issues.t: Headlights shut off from melted wiring
issues.sym: The headlights suddenly go out while driving at night.
issues.why: An owner found melted headlight wiring. Heat at the headlight connectors can burn the plug and cut power.
issues.next: Pull over safely if the lights go out. Have the headlight connectors and wiring inspected and replace any that look brown or melted.

issues.sym: The airbag light stays on while driving.
issues.why: A lit airbag light means the system has stored a fault and the airbags may not work in a crash. Owners had trouble getting dealers to fix it.
issues.next: Have a shop with a scan tool read the airbag codes. Common causes on older cars are a worn clock spring or bad seat wiring.

issues.t: Water leaks onto the passenger floor
issues.sym: Water drips from behind the passenger side of the dash, or the carpet is wet and the windows fog up.
issues.why: A clogged A/C drain hose lets condensation back up into the cabin. A bad windshield or cowl seal can also let rain in.
issues.next: Clear the A/C drain hose under the car and check the cowl and windshield seals. Dry the carpet to avoid mold and electrical problems.

issues.sym: A rattling noise from the engine.
issues.why: One owner reported a rattle. On this engine, a worn timing belt tensioner or idler pulley is a common source, as are loose heat shields.
issues.next: Have a shop find where the noise comes from. If it's the timing belt area, replace the belt and pulleys before they fail.
